source: Owner-requested day-center activity repertoire and flexible front-of-room layout, September 2026. Illustrative rotation, not a verified daily timetable. Monday’s ten sessions are the base loop; Tuesday to Friday rotate a culturally specific repertoire into the same ten 72-second slots.
layoutNote: Three front tables and their twelve chairs are cleared for a flexible activity floor. The original furniture plan remains in the source comparison. Other tables remain for small groups and quieter participation.

programs.label: Performances
programs.title: Familiar songs & community performances
programs.culture: Songs and stories chosen with participants; a bilingual host invites requests.
programs.access: Watch, clap or join in from a chair, wheelchair or standing position.

programs.label: Language circle
programs.title: Language & conversation
programs.culture: Picture prompts, familiar sayings and conversation in preferred languages; Mandarin, Cantonese and English are example options.
programs.access: Listen, point to a picture or speak at your own pace.

programs.label: Device class
programs.title: Everyday device skills
programs.culture: Practice video calls, photos and larger text using step-by-step visual prompts.
programs.access: One-to-one help, a supported tablet and repeatable small steps.

programs.label: Exercise
programs.title: Everyday movement
programs.culture: A staff-led group with familiar music and easy-to-follow demonstrations.
programs.access: Standing, chair-based or wheelchair upper-body movement; rest whenever needed.

programs.label: Dance
programs.title: Music & dance
programs.culture: Participant-selected music, familiar rhythms and a simple shared sequence.
programs.access: Standing steps or seated rhythm and arm movements.

programs.label: Tai chi
programs.title: Tai chi together
programs.culture: Slow, flowing gestures with a visible leader and time to follow.
programs.access: A seated version mirrors the upper-body sequence; a care aide stays nearby.

programs.label: Calligraphy
programs.title: Calligraphy & brushwork
programs.culture: Explore personally meaningful characters and brush strokes, with large sample cards.
programs.access: Thick-handled brushes, supported paper and hand-over-hand help when requested.

programs.label: Arts & crafts
programs.title: Seasonal arts & crafts
programs.culture: Paper, color and collage inspired by the group’s interests and celebrations.
programs.access: Choose, arrange or create with large pieces and individual assistance.

programs.label: Instruments
programs.title: Rhythm & instruments
programs.culture: Simple percussion, listening and shared rhythms around favorite songs.
programs.access: Lightweight shakers and a supported hand drum; listening is welcome.

programs.label: TCM talk
programs.title: TCM & cultural wellness talks
programs.culture: A hosted educational conversation about traditional Chinese medicine, with bilingual discussion and questions.
programs.access: Seated listening, visual prompts and time for questions; a quiet table option stays available.

repertoire.label: Cantonese opera
repertoire.title: Cantonese opera appreciation
repertoire.culture: Recorded and live excerpts from well-loved Cantonese opera; the story of each scene is introduced in Cantonese and English before it plays.
repertoire.access: Listen from any seat with large-print lyric sheets; clapping or humming along is welcome.

repertoire.label: Tea & dim sum social
repertoire.title: Morning tea & dim sum social
repertoire.culture: A relaxed morning table with hot tea and a small dim sum selection planned with the dietitian; conversation is led by whoever has news to share.
repertoire.access: Cups with handles, cut portions and a staff member who serves each table; wheelchairs pull straight up to the table.

repertoire.label: Xiangqi & go
repertoire.title: Xiangqi & go tables
repertoire.culture: Chinese chess and go on large boards, with experienced players paired with newcomers and a game clock nobody enforces.
repertoire.access: Oversized pieces, boards raised to wheelchair height and a staff partner for anyone who prefers to watch a game unfold.

repertoire.label: Qigong
repertoire.title: Qigong · Ba Duan Jin
repertoire.culture: The eight brocades sequence, cued in Cantonese and Mandarin by an instructor who faces the group so each movement can be mirrored.
repertoire.access: Every form has a seated version; a care aide stays within reach of anyone standing.

repertoire.label: Brush painting
repertoire.title: Brush painting · bamboo, plum & birds
repertoire.culture: Ink and wash on rice paper, beginning with bamboo and plum-blossom strokes and moving on to subjects participants suggest.
repertoire.access: Weighted brush handles, taped-down paper and hand-over-hand help when asked for.

repertoire.label: Paper cutting & lanterns
repertoire.title: Paper cutting & lantern making
repertoire.culture: Window flowers, double-happiness cuts and lanterns for Mid-Autumn and Lunar New Year, following patterns participants remember from home.
repertoire.access: Spring-loaded scissors, pre-scored folds and large templates; finished pieces decorate the day room.

repertoire.label: Dumpling & bao demo
repertoire.title: Dumpling & bao making with the dietitian
repertoire.culture: The dietitian and kitchen team fold dumplings and bao with the group, talking through fillings that suit diabetes, low-salt and soft-food plans.
repertoire.access: Seated folding at table height, pre-portioned dough and a tasting for everyone who wants one.

repertoire.label: Chinese knotting
repertoire.title: Chinese knotting
repertoire.culture: Red cord knots for good wishes, from the simple button knot to a shared wall hanging built one section at a time.
repertoire.access: Thick cord, a pegboard to hold tension and small steps demonstrated one at a time.

repertoire.label: Cantopop & Mandopop
repertoire.title: Cantopop & Mandopop sing-along
repertoire.culture: Songs from the Teresa Teng and Sam Hui era through to Beyond, with lyrics on the screen in characters plus jyutping or pinyin, and requests taken all hour.
repertoire.access: Sing, clap or keep time with a shaker; the volume stays comfortable for hearing aids.

repertoire.label: Fan dance
repertoire.title: Fan dance
repertoire.culture: Folk fan-dance steps set to familiar melodies, led slowly enough to learn the opening and closing of the fan together.
repertoire.access: Seated arm and fan movements mirror the standing steps; lightweight fans are provided.

repertoire.label: Story circle
repertoire.title: Reminiscence & story circle
repertoire.culture: Memories of home villages, first jobs and family recipes, shared in Toisanese, Cantonese and Mandarin with staff who speak each.
repertoire.access: Photo prompts and objects to hold; listening counts as taking part.

repertoire.label: Bilingual news
repertoire.title: Bilingual news & current events
repertoire.culture: Headlines from local Chinese-language and English papers, read aloud and discussed side by side, with room for differing views.
repertoire.access: Large-print summaries, one topic at a time and a microphone passed to anyone who wants to comment.

repertoire.label: Planter gardening
repertoire.title: Planter gardening · bok choy, chives & herbs
repertoire.culture: Raised planters of bok choy, garlic chives, Thai basil and mint, tended by the group and harvested for the kitchen.
repertoire.access: Waist-high planters reachable from a wheelchair, long-handled tools and a shaded seat nearby.

repertoire.label: Mindfulness
repertoire.title: Mindfulness & meditation
repertoire.culture: Guided breathing and a quiet body scan, with an optional Buddhist chant or a secular count for those who prefer it.
repertoire.access: Eyes open or closed, seated or in a wheelchair; the room stays dim and no one is asked to speak.

repertoire.label: Birthday of the month
repertoire.title: Birthday of the month
repertoire.culture: Longevity noodles or a shared cake, a birthday song in each guest’s language and a photo for the family board.
repertoire.access: Everyone joins from their own seat; sugar-free and soft options are on the table.

repertoire.label: School visit
repertoire.title: Intergenerational visit from a local school
repertoire.culture: Students from a nearby school bring a prepared song or game, then sit with participants to swap stories about school days then and now.
repertoire.access: Small tables of two or three, an interpreter at each and a quiet corner for anyone who would rather watch.

repertoire.label: Vietnamese folk songs
repertoire.title: Vietnamese folk songs
repertoire.culture: Dân ca and lullabies from the north, centre and south, with a Vietnamese-speaking host and lyrics on the screen.
repertoire.access: Percussion for those who want it and listening for those who do not; the host checks in in Vietnamese.

repertoire.label: Korean, Spanish & Tagalog circles
repertoire.title: Korean, Spanish and Tagalog language circles
repertoire.culture: Three small circles, each hosted by a staff member or volunteer who speaks the language, with news from home and everyday phrases for neighbours.
repertoire.access: Join any circle; picture cards and unhurried speech make it welcoming for beginners.

repertoire.label: Fall-prevention talk
repertoire.title: Fall-prevention health talk in Chinese
repertoire.culture: A nurse or physical therapist explains home hazards, footwear and safe transfers in Cantonese and Mandarin, with a short balance check offered afterwards.
repertoire.access: Seated throughout, printed take-home sheets in Chinese and time to ask about individual situations.

repertoire.label: Tea appreciation
repertoire.title: Tea appreciation · gongfu cha
repertoire.culture: Oolong, pu-erh and jasmine brewed gongfu style at the table, with the origin of each tea and the pour explained in Cantonese and Mandarin.
repertoire.access: Small cups, a warm-not-hot pour and a table height that suits wheelchairs.

repertoire.label: Mahjong strategy
repertoire.title: Mahjong strategy hour
repertoire.culture: Hands, discards and defence talked through at a demonstration table, then open play with Cantonese or Taiwanese rules chosen by each table.
repertoire.access: Large-character tiles, a tile rack for one-handed play and a seat for anyone who prefers to watch.

lunch.source: Illustrative weekly lunch menu planned with the dietitian, not a published menu or a nutrition analysis. Local San Gabriel Valley kitchens cook it; it reaches the center’s kitchen before service and is checked there against each participant’s diet order.

mon.title: Cantonese home cooking
mon.main: Steamed rockfish with ginger and scallion
mon.vegetarian: Lo han jai · braised tofu, shiitake and napa cabbage

adaptations.lowSodium: Steamed rather than sauced; low-sodium soy and ginger-scallion oil come on the side.
adaptations.texture: Boneless fish that flakes for soft & bite-sized, minced with its sauce for minced & moist; congee instead of rice on request.
adaptations.diabetes: Half a scoop of brown rice with extra choy sum; fruit for dessert.

tue.title: Shanghai & Taipei classics
tue.main: Lion’s head meatballs braised with napa cabbage
tue.vegetarian: Taiwanese braised tofu with shiitake and daikon
tue.dessert: Steamed Asian pear with goji berries

adaptations.lowSodium: Meatballs seasoned with ginger, scallion and half the soy; the cabbage carries the flavor.
adaptations.texture: Tender meatballs for soft & bite-sized, minced in their broth for minced & moist; the braised daikon mashes easily.
adaptations.diabetes: A small rice portion with extra bok choy; the pear is steamed without added sugar.

wed.title: A Vietnamese family table
wed.vegetarian: Đậu hũ sốt cà chua · tofu in fresh tomato sauce
wed.soup: Canh chua · tamarind soup with pineapple and tomato
wed.dessert: Chè chuối · banana in warm coconut milk

adaptations.lowSodium: Half the usual fish sauce, balanced with lime and herbs; chili comes on the side.
adaptations.texture: Chicken braised until it shreds, minced in its sauce for minced & moist; no tapioca in the chè for texture diets.
adaptations.diabetes: Chè made with less sugar in a small cup; extra chayote in place of a second scoop of rice.

thu.title: Cocina mexicana
thu.main: Pollo guisado · chicken stewed with tomato, potato and carrot
thu.vegetarian: Enchiladas de frijol with salsa roja and queso fresco

adaptations.lowSodium: Beans cooked from dry without salt pork; salsa and lime on the table instead of extra salt.
adaptations.texture: Chicken that pulls apart for soft & bite-sized, minced in its broth for minced & moist; no tortillas on texture-modified plates.
adaptations.diabetes: Half a portion of rice with extra calabacitas; arroz con leche made with less sugar, or fresh papaya.

fri.title: Korean & Filipino favorites
fri.main: Chicken adobo, made with more vinegar than soy

adaptations.lowSodium: Adobo and dubu-jorim braised with half the soy; a mild cucumber salad stands in for kimchi.
adaptations.texture: Adobo simmered off the bone and shredded in its sauce; tofu is naturally soft; spinach chopped fine for minced & moist.
adaptations.diabetes: Barley rice in a half portion; mango in a small dish.
